metadata.Syllabus Name: AI for Cybersecurity_ Trí tuệ nhân tạo cho an toàn thông tin
metadata.Learning-Teaching Method: In-class lecture, Social Constructivism, Active Learning
metadata.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 54.5h online + 3h offline + 1h final exam + 91.5h self-study
metadata.Description: This course is designed based on the Coursera AI for Cybersecurity Specialization by Johns Hopkins University. The course introduces how artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques are applied to cybersecurity problems, including email threat detection, spam and phishing classification, authentication security, malware detection, network anomaly detection, fraud prevention, adversarial machine learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, reinforcement learning, and AI model evaluation. Students learn to frame cybersecurity problems as data-driven AI tasks, engineer security-relevant features, train and evaluate supervised and unsupervised models, analyze anomalies in network traffic, and assess the robustness of AI systems against adversarial conditions. The course emphasizes defensive, ethical, and responsible applications of AI in cybersecurity through Coursera-based videos, readings, quizzes, hands-on notebooks, and review sessions.
metadata.StudentTasks: Student must complete the online learning activities and get the certificate of AI for Cybersecurity Specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination.
metadata.Tools: Coursera, Jupyter Notebook, Python, common machine learning libraries, course datasets and online quizzes/labs.
metadata.Note:
1. Final Exam included Final Theory Exam (TE): 100%
2. Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.
3. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & (Final TE Score + bonus) >= 5
4. Complete the online courses and get all specialization certifications to be allowed to take Final Exam

metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: This course introduces students to the end to end machine learning lifecycle, focusing on the practices, tools, and culture of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps). Students will learn how to transition machine learning models from isolated experimental notebooks into production-ready, scalable, and continuously monitored software systems. The curriculum covers project scoping, data version control (DVC), automated data and model pipelines (TFX), containerization (Docker), continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), model serving architectures, and automated drift monitoring. By completing hands-on labs and a final capstone project, students will gain engineering skills to build reliable, reproducible, and automated AI systems.

- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.

clos.CLO Details: Explain the core concepts of the MLOps lifecycle, maturity models, and the fundamental architectural differences between DevOps, DataOps, and MLOps.
Execute machine learning project scoping, define business key performance indicators (KPIs), select appropriate deployment patterns, and establish reliable performance baselines.
Implement systematic error analysis, data-centric AI techniques, and experiment tracking to address issues like skewed datasets and class imbalance.
Build automated data pipelines utilizing version control tools (DVC) and centralized feature stores (TFX) to guarantee data lineage and experiment reproducibility.
Design and coordinate end-to-end machine learning orchestration pipelines utilizing components like TensorFlow Extended (TFX) for training, evaluation, and validation.
Apply containerization (Docker) and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) workflows to automate model testing and infrastructure provisioning.
Deploy production-grade model serving microservices using architectures like FastAPI, TensorFlow Serving, and Kubernetes supporting progressive delivery patterns.
Construct automated production monitoring infrastructures with Prometheus, Grafana, and Evidently AI to detect data drift, concept drift, and performance degradation.
Architect, document, and present a complete, end-to-end operational MLOps system that solves a real-world enterprise problem.

metadata.Syllabus Name: Cloud for MLOps_Cloud cho hoạt động học máy
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to design, deploy, and operate end-to-end MLOps pipelines on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). Students will master cloud-native data engineering (S3/GCS, Kafka, Dataflow, Glue), data versioning with DVC, feature stores (Feast, Vertex Feature Store), and scalable model training using distributed GPU/TPU clusters. The curriculum covers CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI), containerization with Docker, Kubernetes-based deployment (GKE/EKS/AKS), and production monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and cloud-native logging. Through hands-on labs and a final cloud-deployed project, students will gain comprehensive experience in building production-ready ML systems with automated monitoring, drift detection, and retraining pipelines, while addressing cost optimization, security, and compliance (GDPR, HIPAA).
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, 4 labs, and 2 process tests assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time.
- Students must complete a final group project (end-to-end MLOps pipeline on cloud) and submit a 4–6 page scientific paper describing the architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis.
- Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes.
- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, ECR, GKE/EKS/AKS), Google Cloud (Vertex AI, Cloud Composer, GCR), Azure (Azure ML, ACR), Docker, Kubernetes, DVC, MLflow, Feast, TFX, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, Evidently AI, FastAPI, TensorFlow Serving.
metadata.Note:
- The course adopts a practice oriented, PBL (project base learning) approach in which students progressively design, deploy, monitor, and maintain an end to end cloud native ML (Machine Learning) system throughout the semester.
- Students complete four hands on laboratory assignments focusing on cloud data versioning and orchestration, TFX pipelines and model validation, containerization and Kubernetes deployment, and monitoring with automated retraining. Labs are completed individually or in assigned teams and submitted before the specified deadlines.
- Two computer based multiple choice Progress Tests evaluate students' theoretical understanding of Cloud MLOps, cloud architecture, data engineering, MLOps pipelines, CI/CD, containerization, deployment, and monitoring concepts.
- Two Process Tests assess practical competencies through production-oriented scenarios, including incident response, drift detection, rollback strategies, model promotion, CI/CD execution, and deployment validation.
- The mandatory team based capstone project requires students to design and implement a complete cloud native MLOps solution, supported by an end-to-end pipeline, technical documentation, cost analysis, a scientific paper, and an in class presentation with a live demonstration.
- The final examination is an individual computer-based multiple choice test covering all major Cloud MLOps concepts and practices.
- The final course grade is calculated as follows: Progress Test 1 (10%), Progress Test 2 (10%), Lab 1 (7.5%), Lab 2 (7.5%), Lab 3 (7.5%), Lab 4 (7.5%), Process Test 1 (7.5%), Process Test 2 (7.5%), Final Project (20%), and Final Examination (10%).
- Completion Criteria: All assessments must score above 0, with a minimum Final Examination score of 4.0 and an overall course grade of 5.0.

clos.CLO Details: Understand core concepts, differences, and relationships among MLOps, DevOps, DataOps, and LLMOps (including RAG & Prompt Engineering basics); apply cloud architecture patterns for ML systems (ingestion, storage, deployment models) across major cloud platforms (AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Vertex AI).

Design and implement cloud-based data engineering pipelines using cloud-native services (AWS Lambda/Step Functions/Glue, GCP Dataflow/Cloud Composer, Azure Data Factory) and implement feature store management solutions (Feast, Vertex/Azure Feature Store) for offline/online inference.

Apply experiment tracking tools (MLflow, WandB, SageMaker Experiments, Vertex Vizier) and data versioning principles using DVC with cloud remotes (S3/GCS/Azure) to ensure reproducibility, data lineage, and metadata management in ML experiments.
Design and build end-to-end TensorFlow Extended (TFX) and cloud native pipelines (including ExampleGen, Transform, Trainer, Evaluator, Publisher), establish model baselines, and handle concept drift.
Understand feature store concepts and implement feature management solutions using Feast, Vertex Feature Store, or Azure Feature Stores for offline/online inference on cloud.

Apply Docker containerization best practices, build containerized MLOps pipelines to deploy to cloud registries (ECR/GCR/ACR) and services (Cloud Run, ECS, GKE, AKS), and implement model serving patterns (TF Serving, FastAPI, Flask) with progressive delivery (blue-green, canary) and autoscaling (HPA/VPA).

Implement automated CI/CD pipelines for ML using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI integrated with cloud services to automate model deployments, testing, and continuous validation in cloud environments.

Implement continuous model monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring) for data/concept drift, setup automated retraining triggers based on performance thresholds, and apply operational excellence principles (incident response, runbooks, rollback, data governance, GDPR, HIPAA, IAM).

Implement an end-to-end Cloud MLOps capstone project encompassing infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, monitoring, automated retraining, and document it via a scientific/technical paper (4–6 pages) detailing architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis.

metadata.Syllabus Name: Advanced MLOps_Hoạt động học máy nâng cao
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to bridge the gap between machine learning model development and production deployment. Students will master essential Python programming for MLOps, explore the integration of DevOps practices, and build efficient microservices, including the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification. The curriculum covers cloud-based data engineering pipelines using AWS technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, Lambda, and SageMaker) alongside industry-standard tools like MLflow and Hugging Face for model tracking, reproducibility, and deployment. Through hands-on projects, students will gain comprehensive experience in designing, building, and managing end-to-end operational pipelines for real-world AI and ML solutions.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, and labs assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time.
- Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes.
- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions), MLflow, Hugging Face, Rust, GitHub.
metadata.Note:
- The mandatory capstone project focuses on designing, implementing, and deploying an end-to-end MLOps system for a real-world machine learning application. Students progressively develop the project through four milestone reports covering infrastructure design, cloud-based data engineering, model lifecycle management, deployment, and final system integration.
- The final mark is calculated by summing the weighted scores of: Progress Test (10%), Report 1 - Infrastructure & Pipeline Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data Engineering & AWS Integration (10%), Report 3 - Model Tracking & Deployment (30%), Report 4 - Final System Report & Group Presentation (10%), and Final Exam - Computer-based Multiple-choice Examination (30%).
- The Progress Test is conducted immediately after the completion of Chapters 1, 2, and 3 to evaluate students' understanding of Python programming, software engineering practices, MLOps methodology, cloud infrastructure, and AWS-based machine learning services.
- Reports 1 to 4 are conducted as in-class group presentations with instructor evaluation and immediate feedback. Each report represents a major milestone of the capstone project and assesses students' practical implementation, documentation quality, system architecture, technical presentation, and teamwork.
- The Final Exam is an individual computer-based multiple-choice examination administered by the examination board. The examination comprehensively evaluates theoretical knowledge and practical concepts from all course chapters, including Python foundations, MLOps methodology, cloud platforms, MLflow, Hugging Face, and production deployment. At least 70% of examination questions must differ from those used in previous semesters.
Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

clos.CLO Details: Understand the core concepts of Python programming, advanced data structures, and their specific applications within MLOps workflows.
Apply clean coding practices, modern testing frameworks, and efficient data manipulation using Pandas and NumPy for machine learning data readiness.
Understand the fundamental principles of MLOps, DevOps, and DataOps methodologies, including their importance in the software development lifecycle.
Design and compose software solutions using microservices architectures and automated operations pipelines to support scalable machine learning applications.
Understand the principles of ethical AI and the application of high-performance languages like Rust for zero-shot classification and efficient processing.
Understand cloud-based data engineering architectures, including data ingestion, repository creation, and secure data transformation solutions.
Apply cloud technologies (such as AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda, and Amazon SageMaker) to build, monitor, and automate end-to-end data engineering and modeling pipelines.
Understand the fundamentals of MLflow, including the Tracking UI, model registries, and artifact management via APIs.
Apply MLflow and Hugging Face modules to package reproducible machine learning projects and deploy pre-trained models efficiently.
Implement an end-to-end Advanced MLOps project that includes infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, and reporting.
